title: Built a browser casino/resort sim with AI, and the hard part turned out to be everything after “make the game”
author: Additional_Touch3082
selftext:
I’ve been building a browser-based casino/resort sim called **Boardwalk Boss** using AI-assisted development, and the project has become a pretty good case study in what “AI game dev” actually looks like once you get past the first prototype.

The game now has three connected modes:

* **Casino Trip**: plan a trip, manage bankroll, play slots, blackjack, video poker, Bingo and other activities, earn rewards/status, and explore the resort.
* **Career Mode**: start working at the property and move through management roles all the way to CEO.
* **Owner Mode**: run the resort, manage finances/staffing/projects, compete in the market, build a second tower, acquire another property, and manage a small hospitality portfolio.

There are also side systems like a coastal executive home, a 3-hole golf mini-game, achievements, scenarios, Resort Explorer, persistent save states, and resort visuals that change as projects are completed.

What surprised me most is how little of the work is actually “generate a feature and move on.”

Most of the effort has been:

* catching state/save bugs
* removing redundant flows
* fixing mobile/tablet behavior
* reducing clicks
* making systems feel coherent across multiple modes
* validating economics
* keeping UI from looking generically AI-generated
* managing bundle size/performance
* building review fixtures so weird late-game states can be tested without playing for hours
* repeatedly reworking visual direction after hands-on testing

I’m using AI heavily, but not as a one-shot “build this game” tool. It’s much closer to a loop of **design → implement → test → break → inspect → simplify → polish**.

It’s playable now at **boardwalkboss.com**.

Would be interested in hearing from others doing AI-assisted game development, especially around where you’ve found AI genuinely accelerates development versus where it tends to create cleanup debt later.
